#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -u
export LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 TZ=UTC

BIN=/tmp/search_index_coderl_acceptance
( cd /workspace/repo/searchIndex && go build -o "$BIN" . ) \
    || { echo "FAIL: build" >&2; exit 1; }

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
SONIC_PID=""
trap 'stop_sonic 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cd "$TMP" || exit 1

fail() { echo "FAIL: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

assert_contains() {
    local needle=$1 file=$2 label=$3
    grep -Fq "$needle" "$file" || fail "$label: missing [$needle]"
}

assert_not_contains() {
    local needle=$1 file=$2 label=$3
    if grep -Fq "$needle" "$file"; then
        fail "$label: unexpected [$needle]"
    fi
}

assert_log_contains() {
    local needle=$1 label=$2

    grep -Fq "$needle" out || grep -Fq "$needle" err || fail "$label: missing log [$needle]"
}

assert_log_not_contains() {
    local needle=$1 label=$2

    if grep -Fq "$needle" out || grep -Fq "$needle" err; then
        fail "$label: unexpected log [$needle]"
    fi
}

write_conf() {
    local path=$1 root=$2 posts=$3 collection=$4 bucket=$5
    cat > "$path" <<EOF
sonic_host: 127.0.0.1
sonic_password: SecretPassword
sonic_collection: $collection
sonic_bucket: $bucket
root_path: $root
post_path: $posts
index_all_init: true
EOF
}

start_sonic() {
    local mode=$1 log=$2 ready=$3
    rm -f "$log" "$ready"
    python3 /workspace/repo/usercase-test-coderl/fixtures/fake_sonic.py \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 1491 --log "$log" --ready "$ready" --mode "$mode" &
    SONIC_PID=$!
    for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
        [ -f "$ready" ] && return 0
        sleep 0.05
    done
    fail "fake Sonic did not start"
}

stop_sonic() {
    if [ -n "${SONIC_PID:-}" ]; then
        kill "$SONIC_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$SONIC_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
        SONIC_PID=""
    fi
}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import argparse
+import socket
+import threading
+
+
+def append_line(path, line):
+    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        handle.write(line + "\n")
+        handle.flush()
+
+
+def handle_client(conn, log_path, mode):
+    with conn:
+        conn.sendall(b"CONNECTED mock-sonic\r\n")
+        stream = conn.makefile("rwb", buffering=0)
+        while True:
+            raw = stream.readline()
+            if not raw:
+                return
+            line = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").rstrip("\r\n")
+            append_line(log_path, line)
+
+            if line.startswith("START "):
+                stream.write(b"STARTED ingest protocol(1) buffer(20000)\r\n")
+            elif line.startswith("FLUSHO "):
+                stream.write(b"OK\r\n")
+            elif line.startswith("PUSH "):
+                if mode == "push_error":
+                    stream.write(b"ERR rejected by fake sonic\r\n")
+                else:
+                    stream.write(b"OK\r\n")
+            elif line == "QUIT":
+                stream.write(b"ENDED\r\n")
+                return
+            elif line == "PING":
+                stream.write(b"PONG\r\n")
+            else:
+                stream.write(b"OK\r\n")
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
+    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=1491)
+    parser.add_argument("--log", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--ready", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["ok", "push_error"], default="ok")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    open(args.log, "w", encoding="utf-8").close()
+    server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+    server.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
+    server.bind((args.host, args.port))
+    server.listen(32)
+    with open(args.ready, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        handle.write("ready\n")
+
+    try:
+        while True:
+            conn, _ = server.accept()
+            thread = threading.Thread(
+                target=handle_client, args=(conn, args.log, args.mode), daemon=True
+            )
+            thread.start()
+    finally:
+        server.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -525,6 +525,46 @@ class TestBarrier:
 
         assert optimized_gates == 2
 
+    def test_barrier_adjoint_returns_equivalent_barrier(self):
+        """Test that the adjoint transform can handle an isolated Barrier operation."""
+        wires = ["alpha", "beta"]
+        expected_operation = qml.Barrier(only_visual=False, wires=wires)
+
+        with qml.tape.QuantumTape() as tape:
+            qml.adjoint(qml.Barrier)(only_visual=False, wires=wires)
+
+        assert len(tape.operations) == 1
+        adjoint_operation = tape.operations[0]
+        assert type(adjoint_operation) is type(expected_operation)
+        assert adjoint_operation.wires == expected_operation.wires
+        assert adjoint_operation.only_visual is expected_operation.only_visual
+
+    def test_adjoint_function_preserves_barrier_on_same_wires(self):
+        """Test that Barrier is preserved when adjointing a quantum function."""
+
+        def qfunc():
+            qml.Hadamard(wires="left")
+            qml.Barrier(only_visual=False, wires=["left", "right"])
+            qml.CNOT(wires=["left", "right"])
+
+        expected_operation_types = [qml.Hadamard, qml.Barrier, qml.CNOT]
+
+        with qml.tape.QuantumTape() as tape:
+            qfunc()
+            qml.adjoint(qfunc)()
+
+        operations = tape.operations
+
+        assert [type(op) for op in operations] == [
+            *expected_operation_types,
+            *reversed(expected_operation_types),
+        ]
+
+        original_barrier = operations[1]
+        adjointed_barrier = operations[4]
+        assert adjointed_barrier.wires == original_barrier.wires
+        assert adjointed_barrier.only_visual is original_barrier.only_visual
+
 
 class TestMultiControlledX:
     """Tests for the MultiControlledX"""

+import inspect

+)
+
+REPRESENTATIVE_TRAIT_CHECKS = {
+    "PlotLabel": ("text",),

+    "StatusLayer": (),
+}
+
+NO_ARG_CONSTRUCTIBLE_EXPORTS = (
+    "PlotLabel",
+    "DataLabel",
+    "SimpleInspectorOverlay",
+)
+
+
+def _assert_traits_public_class(obj, name):
+    assert inspect.isclass(obj), f"{name} should be a class"
+    assert hasattr(obj, "class_traits"), f"{name} should be a Traits class"
+    assert obj.class_traits(), f"{name} should expose Traits metadata"
+
+
+def test_overlays_api_exports_overlay_classes():
+    import chaco.overlays.api as overlays_api
+
+    for name in CLASS_EXPORTS:
+        obj = getattr(overlays_api, name)
+        _assert_traits_public_class(obj, name)
+
+
+def test_overlays_api_exports_formatter_helpers():
+    import chaco.overlays.api as overlays_api
+
+    for name in FORMATTER_EXPORTS:
+        obj = getattr(overlays_api, name)
+        assert callable(obj), f"{name} should be callable"
+
+
+def test_chaco_api_reexports_overlay_classes():
+    import chaco.api as chaco_api
+
+    for name in CLASS_EXPORTS:
+        obj = getattr(chaco_api, name)
+        _assert_traits_public_class(obj, name)
+
+
+def test_chaco_api_reexports_formatter_helpers():

+
+    for name in FORMATTER_EXPORTS:
+        obj = getattr(chaco_api, name)
+        assert callable(obj), f"{name} should be callable"
+
+
+def test_chaco_api_and_overlays_api_objects_are_identical():
+    import chaco.api as chaco_api
+    import chaco.overlays.api as overlays_api
+
+    for name in CLASS_EXPORTS + FORMATTER_EXPORTS:
+        assert getattr(chaco_api, name) is getattr(overlays_api, name)
+
+
+def test_representative_exports_are_real_traits_classes():
+    import chaco.overlays.api as overlays_api
+
+    for name, required_traits in REPRESENTATIVE_TRAIT_CHECKS.items():
+        cls = getattr(overlays_api, name)

[ "$(grep -c '^<Error>$' "$REPORT3" || true)" -eq 0 ] || fail "F3 clean report contains Error blocks"

[ ! -e "$BAD_REPORT" ] || fail "F4 report should not exist"

echo "PASS"
exit 0

# Generate parser if missing

    mkdir -p bin

    bin/goyacc -o /dev/null -xegen temp_parser_file parser/parser.y
    bin/goyacc -o parser/parser.go -xe temp_parser_file parser/parser.y

with open('parser/parser.go', 'rb') as f:
    data = f.read()
fixed = data.replace(b'\xef\xbf', b' ')
with open('parser/parser.go', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(fixed)
" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Run executor tests
export GO111MODULE=off
export GOPATH=/testbed/_vendor:/root/go
export CGO_ENABLED=1

+import importlib.util
+import os
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+import versioneer
+
+
+def load_runtime_version_module():
+    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__)),
+                        "pyemma", "_version.py")
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("pyemma_runtime_version", path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+class VersioneerResilienceTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.runtime = load_runtime_version_module()
+        self.root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="versioneer-test-")
+        open(os.path.join(self.root, ".git"), "w").close()
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        os.unlink(os.path.join(self.root, ".git"))
+        os.rmdir(self.root)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def runner(describe, full="0123456789abcdef", count="7"):
+        def run(commands, args, cwd=None, **kwargs):
+            if args[0] == "describe":
+                return describe
+            if args[0] == "rev-parse":
+                return full
+            if args[0] == "rev-list":
+                return count
+            raise AssertionError("unexpected command: %r" % (args,))
+        return run
+
+    def test_tagged_history_keeps_existing_shape_in_both_copies(self):
+        run = self.runner("v2.4-3-gabcdef0-dirty")
+        expected = {
+            "closest-tag": "2.4",
+            "distance": 3,
+            "short": "abcdef0",
+            "dirty": True,
+            "long": "0123456789abcdef",
+            "error": None,
+        }
+        self.assertEqual(versioneer.git_pieces_from_vcs("v", self.root, False, run), expected)
+        self.assertEqual(self.runtime.git_pieces_from_vcs("v", self.root, False, run), expected)
+
+    def test_untagged_history_uses_numeric_count_in_both_copies(self):
+        run = self.runner("abcdef0", count="12\n")
+        for module in (versioneer, self.runtime):
+            pieces = module.git_pieces_from_vcs("v", self.root, False, run)
+            self.assertIsNone(pieces["closest-tag"])
+            self.assertEqual(pieces["distance"], 12)
+            self.assertEqual(pieces["short"], "0123456")
+            self.assertIsNone(pieces["error"])
+
+    def test_missing_count_is_a_structured_error_not_an_exception(self):
+        run = self.runner("abcdef0", count=None)
+        for module in (versioneer, self.runtime):
+            try:
+                pieces = module.git_pieces_from_vcs("v", self.root, False, run)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                self.fail("git metadata failure should be returned as error data: %s" % exc)
+            self.assertIsNone(pieces["closest-tag"])
+            self.assertIsNone(pieces.get("distance"))
+            self.assertIsInstance(pieces["error"], str)
+            rendered = module.render(pieces, "pep440")
+            self.assertEqual(rendered["version"], "unknown")
+            self.assertEqual(rendered["error"], pieces["error"])
+
+    def test_non_numeric_count_is_a_structured_error_not_an_exception(self):
+        run = self.runner("abcdef0", count="not-a-count")
+        for module in (versioneer, self.runtime):
+            try:
+                pieces = module.git_pieces_from_vcs("v", self.root, False, run)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                self.fail("git metadata failure should be returned as error data: %s" % exc)
+            self.assertIsInstance(pieces["error"], str)
+            self.assertTrue(pieces["error"].strip())
+
+    def test_public_build_lookup_falls_back_when_provider_raises(self):
+        original_keywords = versioneer.HANDLERS["git"]["keywords"]
+        original_vcs = versioneer.HANDLERS["git"]["pieces_from_vcs"]
+        try:
+            versioneer.HANDLERS["git"]["keywords"] = lambda *a: (_ for _ in ()).throw(versioneer.NotThisMethod())
+            versioneer.HANDLERS["git"]["pieces_from_vcs"] = lambda *a: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError("bad count"))
+            try:
+                result = versioneer.get_versions()
+            except Exception as exc:
+                self.fail("public lookup should degrade to unknown version: %s" % exc)
+        finally:
+            versioneer.HANDLERS["git"]["keywords"] = original_keywords
+            versioneer.HANDLERS["git"]["pieces_from_vcs"] = original_vcs
+        self.assertEqual(result["version"], "0+unknown")
+        self.assertIsNotNone(result["error"])
+
+    def test_public_runtime_lookup_falls_back_when_provider_raises(self):
+        original_keywords = self.runtime.git_versions_from_keywords
+        original_vcs = self.runtime.git_pieces_from_vcs
+        try:
+            self.runtime.git_versions_from_keywords = lambda *a: (_ for _ in ()).throw(self.runtime.NotThisMethod())
+            self.runtime.git_pieces_from_vcs = lambda *a: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError("bad count"))
+            try:
+                result = self.runtime.get_versions()
+            except Exception as exc:
+                self.fail("public lookup should degrade to unknown version: %s" % exc)
+        finally:
+            self.runtime.git_versions_from_keywords = original_keywords
+            self.runtime.git_pieces_from_vcs = original_vcs

import json

if stripped in ("", "[]"):

    raise SystemExit(0)

entries = []
cur = None
in_import = False

def finish():
    if cur is not None:
        entries.append(cur)

for raw in text.splitlines():
    line = raw.rstrip()
    if not line:
        continue
    if line.startswith("- image:"):
        finish()
        image = line[len("- image:"):].strip()
        if not image:
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: empty image name")
        cur = {"image": image}
        in_import = False
    elif cur is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: graph output must start with an image entry, got {line!r}")
    elif line == "  dependsOn:":
        cur.setdefault("dependsOn", {})
        in_import = False
    elif line.startswith("    from:"):
        cur.setdefault("dependsOn", {})["from"] = line[len("    from:"):].strip()
        in_import = False
    elif line == "    import:":
        cur.setdefault("dependsOn", {})["import"] = []

    elif in_import and line.startswith("    - "):
        cur.setdefault("dependsOn", {}).setdefault("import", []).append(line[len("    - "):].strip())
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: unexpected graph line {line!r}")

finish()

PY

--- /dev/null
+++ b/usercase-test-coderl/test_cardinality_rule_stateful.py
@@ -0,0 +1,252 @@
+import datetime
+
+import pytest
+
+from elastalert.ruletypes import CardinalityRule
+from elastalert.util import EAException
+
+
+BASE = datetime.datetime(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)
+TIMEFRAME = datetime.timedelta(minutes=10)
+
+
+def at(minutes=0, seconds=0):
+    return BASE + datetime.timedelta(minutes=minutes, seconds=seconds)
+
+
+def assert_one_match(rule):
+    assert len(rule.matches) == 1
+    return rule.matches[0]
+
+
+def assert_timestamp_equivalent(value, expected):
+    if isinstance(value, datetime.datetime):
+        actual = value
+    else:
+        actual = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(str(value).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+    if actual.tzinfo is not None:
+        actual = actual.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
+    assert actual == expected
+
+
+def assert_cardinality_message(message, kind, threshold, field):
+    assert isinstance(message, str)
+    text = message.strip().lower()
+    assert text
+    assert str(threshold) in text
+    assert field.lower() in text
+    if kind == "max":
+        assert any(token in text for token in ("max", "maximum", "above", "greater", "higher", "exceed"))
+    else:
+        assert any(token in text for token in ("min", "minimum", "below", "less", "lower", "under"))
+    assert any(token in text for token in ("timeframe", "window", "between", "since", "minute", "hour"))
+
+
+def max_rules(**overrides):
+    rules = {
+        "max_cardinality": 4,
+        "timeframe": TIMEFRAME,
+        "cardinality_field": "user",
+        "timestamp_field": "@timestamp",
+    }
+    rules.update(overrides)
+    return rules
+
+
+def min_rules(**overrides):
+    rules = {
+        "min_cardinality": 4,
+        "timeframe": TIMEFRAME,
+        "cardinality_field": "user",
+        "timestamp_field": "@timestamp",
+    }
+    rules.update(overrides)
+    return rules
+
+
+def test_max_cardinality_session_alerts_only_on_fifth_distinct_value():
+
+
+
+    rule = CardinalityRule(max_rules())
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    for minute, user in enumerate(["bill", "coach", "zoey", "louis"]):
+        rule.add_data([{"@timestamp": at(minute), "user": user, "seq": minute}])
+        assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.add_data([{"@timestamp": at(4), "user": "coach", "seq": 4}])
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.add_data([{"@timestamp": at(5), "user": "francis", "seq": 5}])
+
+    match = assert_one_match(rule)
+    assert match["user"] == "francis"
+    assert match["seq"] == 5
+    assert_timestamp_equivalent(match["@timestamp"], at(5))
+
+    assert_cardinality_message(rule.get_match_str(match), "max", 4, "user")
+
+
+def test_min_cardinality_session_waits_until_timeframe_elapsed():
+
+
+
+    rule = CardinalityRule(min_rules())
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.add_data(
+        [
+            {"@timestamp": at(0), "user": "bill"},
+            {"@timestamp": at(1), "user": "coach"},
+        ]
+    )
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.garbage_collect(at(10))
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.garbage_collect(at(10, 1))
+
+    match = assert_one_match(rule)
+    assert_timestamp_equivalent(match["@timestamp"], at(10, 1))
+
+    assert_cardinality_message(rule.get_match_str(match), "min", 4, "user")
+
+
+def test_query_key_dotted_field_missing_values_and_duplicates_are_isolated():
+
+
+
+    rule = CardinalityRule(
+        max_rules(max_cardinality=2, cardinality_field="d.ip", query_key="user")
+    )
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    for event in [
+        {"@timestamp": at(0), "user": "zoey", "d": {"ip": "10.0.0.1"}, "seq": 1},
+        {"@timestamp": at(1), "user": "coach", "d": {"ip": "10.0.1.1"}, "seq": 2},
+        {"@timestamp": at(2), "user": "zoey", "d": {"ip": "10.0.0.2"}, "seq": 3},
+        {"@timestamp": at(3), "user": "coach", "d": {"ip": "10.0.1.1"}, "seq": 4},
+        {"@timestamp": at(4), "user": "coach", "seq": 5},
+        {"@timestamp": at(5), "user": "coach", "d": {"ip": "10.0.1.2"}, "seq": 6},
+    ]:
+        rule.add_data([event])
+        assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.add_data(
+        [{"@timestamp": at(6), "user": "coach", "d": {"ip": "10.0.1.3"}, "seq": 7}]
+    )
+
+    match = assert_one_match(rule)
+    assert match["user"] == "coach"
+    assert match["d"]["ip"] == "10.0.1.3"
+    assert_timestamp_equivalent(match["@timestamp"], at(6))
+
+    assert_cardinality_message(rule.get_match_str(match), "max", 2, "d.ip")
+
+
+def test_garbage_collect_expires_values_before_next_max_cardinality_window():
+
+
+
+    rule = CardinalityRule(max_rules(max_cardinality=2))
+    rule.add_data(
+        [
+            {"@timestamp": at(0), "user": "bill", "seq": 1},
+            {"@timestamp": at(1), "user": "coach", "seq": 2},
+        ]
+    )
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.garbage_collect(at(12))
+    assert rule.matches == []
+
+    rule.add_data([{"@timestamp": at(12), "user": "zoey", "seq": 3}])
+    assert rule.matches == []
+    rule.add_data([{"@timestamp": at(13), "user": "louis", "seq": 4}])
+    assert rule.matches == []
+    rule.add_data([{"@timestamp": at(14), "user": "francis", "seq": 5}])
+
+    match = assert_one_match(rule)
+    assert match["user"] == "francis"
+    assert match["seq"] == 5
+    assert_timestamp_equivalent(match["@timestamp"], at(14))
+
+
+def test_constructor_requires_a_cardinality_threshold():
+
+
+
+    with pytest.raises(EAException) as excinfo:
+        CardinalityRule(
+            {
+                "timeframe": TIMEFRAME,
+                "cardinality_field": "user",
+                "timestamp_field": "@timestamp",
+            }
+        )
+
+
+    assert isinstance(excinfo.value, EAException)
+
+
+def test_repeated_garbage_collect_at_same_timestamp_is_idempotent():

+import os
+import shutil
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+from mypy.stubgen import generate_stub
+from mypy.stubgenc import generate_c_function_stub, generate_c_type_stub
+
+
+def _gen_py_stub(source):
+    tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
+    try:
+        src_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'mod.py')
+        with open(src_path, 'w') as f:
+            f.write(source)
+        out_dir = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'out')
+        os.makedirs(out_dir)
+        generate_stub(src_path, out_dir)
+        with open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'mod.py')) as f:
+            return f.read()
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(tmpdir)
+
+
+class StubgenPyEllipsisTests(unittest.TestCase):
+
+
+    def test_function_body_uses_ellipsis(self):
+        out = _gen_py_stub('def f():\n    x = 1\n')
+        self.assertIn('def f(): ...', out)
+        self.assertNotIn(': pass', out)
+
+    def test_function_with_args_uses_ellipsis(self):
+        out = _gen_py_stub('def f(a, b=2): return 1\n')
+        self.assertIn('def f(a, b=2): ...', out)
+        self.assertNotIn('pass', out)
+
+    def test_empty_class_uses_ellipsis(self):
+        out = _gen_py_stub('class A: pass\n')
+        self.assertIn('class A: ...', out)
+        self.assertNotIn(': pass', out)
+
+    def test_empty_class_with_base_uses_ellipsis(self):
+        out = _gen_py_stub('class A: pass\nclass B(A): pass\n')
+        self.assertIn('class A: ...', out)
+        self.assertIn('class B(A): ...', out)
+        self.assertNotIn(': pass', out)
+
+    def test_method_inside_class_uses_ellipsis(self):
+        out = _gen_py_stub('class A:\n    def m(self, x): return x\n')
+
+        self.assertIn('def m(self, x): ...', out)
+        self.assertNotIn('pass', out)
+
+    def test_class_made_empty_after_stripping_uses_ellipsis(self):
+
+        out = _gen_py_stub('class A:\n    def _f(self): pass\n')
+        self.assertIn('class A: ...', out)
+        self.assertNotIn(': pass', out)

+from mystic.math.measures import (
+    expectation,
+    expected_variance,
+    impose_expected_mean_and_variance,
+)
+
+
+def identity_model(x):
+    return x[0]
+
+
+def sum_model(x):
+    return x[0] + x[1]
+
+
+def weighted_linear_model(x):
+    return x[0] + 2 * x[1]
+
+
+def rounded_axis_constraints(coords, weights):
+    return [[round(value, 1) for value in axis] for axis in coords]
+
+
+def call_impose(param, f, npts, bounds=None, weights=None, **kwds):
+    options = {
+        "debug": True,
+        "npop": kwds.pop("npop", 20),
+        "maxiter": kwds.pop("maxiter", 100),
+        "maxfun": kwds.pop("maxfun", 10000),
+    }
+    options.update(kwds)
+    with redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
+        return impose_expected_mean_and_variance(
+            param, f, npts, bounds=bounds, weights=weights, **options
+        )
+
+
+def float_samples(samples):
+    return [tuple(float(value) for value in sample) for sample in samples]
+
+
+def _product(values):
+    result = 1
+    for value in values:
+        result *= value
+    return result
+
+
+def _tolerances(param, tol):
+    if tol is None:
+        value = 0.01 * max(param)
+        return value, value
+    if isinstance(tol, tuple):
+        mean_tol, variance_tol = tol
+        default = 0.01 * max(param)
+        return mean_tol or default, variance_tol or default
+    return tol, tol
+
+
+def _bounds_lists(bounds):
+    if isinstance(bounds, Bounds):
+        return bounds.xlower, bounds.xupper
+    return bounds
+
+
+def assert_samples_meet_spec(samples, f, npts, bounds, weights, param, tol=None):
+
+
+    assert isinstance(samples, list)
+    assert len(samples) == _product(npts)
+    for sample in samples:
+        assert isinstance(sample, tuple)
+        assert len(sample) == len(npts)
+
+    lower, upper = _bounds_lists(bounds)
+    assert len(lower) == sum(npts)
+    assert len(upper) == sum(npts)
+    for sample in samples:
+        for value in sample:
+            assert min(lower) <= float(value) <= max(upper)
+
+    mean_tol, variance_tol = _tolerances(param, tol)
+    assert abs(float(expectation(f, samples, weights)) - param[0]) <= mean_tol
+    assert abs(float(expected_variance(f, samples, weights)) - param[1]) <= variance_tol
+
+
+def test_scalar_tolerance_tuple_bounds_one_dimensional_identity_model():
+
+
+
+
+    weights = [0.5, 0.5]
+
+    samples = call_impose(
+        (1.0, 0.25),
+        identity_model,
+        (2,),

+        weights,
+        (1.0, 0.25),
+        tol=0.05,
+    )
+
+
+def test_pair_tolerance_product_measure_sum_model():
+
+
+
+
+    weights = [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25]
+
+    samples = call_impose(
+        (2.0, 0.5),
+        sum_model,
+        (2, 2),

+        tol=(0.1, 0.1),

+        (2, 2),

+        (2.0, 0.5),
+        tol=(0.1, 0.1),
+    )
+
+
+def test_bounds_object_nonuniform_weights_and_default_tolerance():
+
+
+
+
+    weights = [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]
+
+    samples = call_impose(
+        (3.0, 0.2),
+        weighted_linear_model,
+        (2, 2),
+        bounds=Bounds([0.0, 0.0], [2.0, 2.0], n=(2, 2)),
+        weights=weights,
+        npop=30,
+        maxiter=150,
+        maxfun=20000,
+    )
+
+    assert_samples_meet_spec(
+        samples,

+
+
+

+

+package ratelimit_test
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"net"
+	"os/exec"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	goredis "github.com/go-redis/redis/v8"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"github.com/unkeyed/unkey/apps/agent/pkg/ratelimit"
+)
+
+func TestRedisRateLimiterTokenBucket(t *testing.T) {
+	redisURL := startLocalRedis(t)
+
+	rl, err := ratelimit.NewRedis(ratelimit.RedisConfig{
+		RedisUrl: redisURL,
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	req := ratelimit.RatelimitRequest{
+		Identifier:     "token-bucket-smoke-" + uniqueTestID(t),
+		Max:            3,
+		RefillRate:     1,
+		RefillInterval: 50,
+	}
+
+	for wantRemaining := int32(2); wantRemaining >= 0; wantRemaining-- {
+		res := rl.Take(req)
+		require.True(t, res.Pass)
+		require.Equal(t, req.Max, res.Limit)
+		require.Equal(t, wantRemaining, res.Remaining)
+	}
+
+	res := rl.Take(req)
+	require.False(t, res.Pass)
+	require.Equal(t, req.Max, res.Limit)
+	require.Equal(t, int32(0), res.Remaining)
+
+	time.Sleep(time.Until(time.UnixMilli(res.Reset).Add(10 * time.Millisecond)))
+
+	refilled := rl.Take(req)
+	require.True(t, refilled.Pass)
+	require.Equal(t, int32(0), refilled.Remaining)
+}
+
+func startLocalRedis(t *testing.T) string {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	port := freeLocalPort(t)
+	cmd := exec.Command("redis-server",
+		"--save", "",
+		"--appendonly", "no",
+		"--bind", "127.0.0.1",
+		"--port", fmt.Sprintf("%d", port),
+	)
+	require.NoError(t, cmd.Start())
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		_ = cmd.Process.Kill()
+		_ = cmd.Wait()
+	})
+
+	url := fmt.Sprintf("redis://127.0.0.1:%d", port)
+	client := goredis.NewClient(&goredis.Options{Addr: fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port)})
+	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = client.Close() })
+
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
+	for {
+		if err := client.Ping(context.Background()).Err(); err == nil {
+			return url
+		}
+		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
+			t.Fatalf("redis-server did not become ready on %s", url)
+		}
+		time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+}
+
+func freeLocalPort(t *testing.T) int {
+	t.Helper()
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	defer ln.Close()
+	return ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port
+}
+
+func uniqueTestID(t *testing.T) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	return fmt.Sprintf("%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
+}

+

+	bpm   float64
+}
+
+func writeSilentWAV(t *testing.T, path string, seconds float64) {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	const sampleRate = 44100
+	frames := int(math.Round(seconds * sampleRate))
+	dataBytes := frames * 2
+
+	f, err := os.Create(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("create wav: %v", err)
+	}
+	defer f.Close()
+
+	mustWrite := func(data any) {
+		t.Helper()
+		var err error
+		switch v := data.(type) {
+		case []byte:
+			_, err = f.Write(v)
+		default:
+			err = binary.Write(f, binary.LittleEndian, v)
+		}
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("write wav: %v", err)
+		}
+	}
+
+	mustWrite([]byte("RIFF"))
+	mustWrite(uint32(36 + dataBytes))
+	mustWrite([]byte("WAVE"))
+	mustWrite([]byte("fmt "))
+	mustWrite(uint32(16))
+	mustWrite(uint16(1))
+	mustWrite(uint16(1))
+	mustWrite(uint32(sampleRate))
+	mustWrite(uint32(sampleRate * 2))
+	mustWrite(uint16(2))
+	mustWrite(uint16(16))
+	mustWrite([]byte("data"))
+	mustWrite(uint32(dataBytes))
+	mustWrite(make([]byte, dataBytes))
+}
+
+func makeWAV(t *testing.T, name string, seconds float64) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), name)
+	writeSilentWAV(t, path, seconds)
+	return path
+}
+
+func assertTiming(t *testing.T, path string, expected expectedTiming) {
+	t.Helper()
+	beats, bpm, err := getbpm.GetBPM(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("GetBPM(%q) err = %v", path, err)
+	}
+
+	if math.Abs(beats-expected.beats) > 0.25 || math.Abs(bpm-expected.bpm) > 0.25 {
+		t.Fatalf("GetBPM(%q) = beats %.10f bpm %.10f, want about beats %.10f bpm %.10f", path, beats, bpm, expected.beats, expected.bpm)
+	}
+}
+
+func assertEqualSlices(t *testing.T, onsets []float64, duration float64, slices int) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if len(onsets) != slices {
+		t.Fatalf("onsets length = %d, want inferred slice count %d", len(onsets), slices)
+	}
+	if slices == 0 {
+		return
+	}
+	if math.Abs(onsets[0]) > 1e-9 {
+		t.Fatalf("first equal slice = %.10f, want 0", onsets[0])
+	}
+	step := duration / float64(slices)
+	for i, onset := range onsets {
+		want := float64(i) * step
+		if math.Abs(onset-want) > 1e-6 {

+import tempfile

+from pathlib import Path
+
+from hypothesistooling import releasemanagement as rm
+
+
+class ReleaseContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def assert_result(self, expected, function, *args):
+        try:
+            actual = function(*args)
+        except Exception as error:
+            self.fail("unexpected %s: %s" % (type(error).__name__, error))
+        self.assertEqual(actual, expected)
+
+    def assert_value_error(self, function, *args):
+        try:
+            function(*args)
+        except ValueError:
+            return
+        except Exception as error:
+            self.fail("expected ValueError, got %s: %s" % (type(error).__name__, error))
+        self.fail("expected ValueError")
+
+    def test_release_header_accepts_bom_whitespace_and_crlf(self):
+        contents = "\ufeff  RELEASE_TYPE:  minor  \r\n\r\nAdd feature.  \r\n"
+        self.assert_result(("minor", "Add feature."), rm.parse_release_file_contents, contents, "release")
+
+    def test_release_header_rejects_trailing_directive_text(self):
+        for header in (
+            "RELEASE_TYPE: patch extra\nnotes",
+            "RELEASE_TYPE: major # comment\nnotes",
+            "RELEASE_TYPE: minor\ttrailing\nnotes",
+        ):
+            self.assert_value_error(rm.parse_release_file_contents, header, "release")
+
+    def test_release_body_strips_line_endings_without_destroying_indentation(self):
+        contents = "RELEASE_TYPE: patch\n\n  bullet\t \n\n    continuation\n\n"
+        self.assert_result(
+            ("patch", "  bullet\n\n    continuation"),
+            rm.parse_release_file_contents,
+            contents,
+            "release",
+        )
+
+    def test_release_header_errors_include_missing_and_unknown_types(self):
+        for contents in ("", "notes first\n", "RELEASE_TYPE: feature\nnotes"):
+            self.assert_value_error(rm.parse_release_file_contents, contents, "release.md")
+
+    def test_extract_assignment_rejects_duplicate_exact_assignments(self):
+        self.assert_value_error(
+            rm.extract_assignment_from_string, "version = '1'\nversion='2'", "version"
+        )
+        self.assert_result(
+            "'2'", rm.extract_assignment_from_string, "myversion = '1'\nversion='2'", "version"
+        )
+
+    def test_replace_assignment_preserves_crlf_and_terminal_newline(self):
+        source = "  version = '1'\r\nother=2\r\n"
+        self.assert_result(
+            "  version = '3'\r\nother=2\r\n",
+            rm.replace_assignment_in_string,
+            source,
+            "version",
+            "'3'",
+        )
+
+    def test_replace_assignment_preserves_lf_without_terminal_newline(self):
+        source = "version=1\nother = 2"
+        self.assert_result(
+            "version=3\nother = 2",
+            rm.replace_assignment_in_string,
+            source,
+            "version",
+            "3",
+        )
+
+    def test_replace_assignment_rejects_missing_and_duplicate_targets(self):
+        for source in ("other = 1\n", "version=1\nversion=2\n"):
+            self.assert_value_error(rm.replace_assignment_in_string, source, "version", "3")
+
+    def test_parse_version_requires_three_nonnegative_integer_components(self):
+        self.assert_result((1, 20, 3), rm.parse_version, "1.20.3")
+        self.assert_result((0, 0, 0), rm.parse_version, "0.0.0")
+        for value in (
+            "1.2",
+            "1.2.3.4",
+            "1.-2.3",
+            "01.2.3",
+            "1.2.x",
+            " 1.2.3",
+            "1.2.3 ",
+        ):
+            self.assert_value_error(rm.parse_version, value)
+
+    def test_bump_version_updates_requested_component_and_resets_lower(self):
+        self.assert_result(("1.2.4", (1, 2, 4)), rm.bump_version_info, (1, 2, 3), "patch")
+        self.assert_result(("1.3.0", (1, 3, 0)), rm.bump_version_info, (1, 2, 3), "minor")
+        self.assert_result(("2.0.0", (2, 0, 0)), rm.bump_version_info, (1, 2, 3), "major")
+
+    def test_bump_version_rejects_invalid_release_type_or_shape(self):
+        for version, release_type in (
+            ((1, 2), "patch"),
+            ((1, -1, 0), "minor"),
+            ((1, 2, 3), "feature"),
+            ((1, 2.0, 3), "patch"),
+        ):
+            self.assert_value_error(rm.bump_version_info, version, release_type)
+
+    def test_changelog_update_prepends_entry_and_preserves_previous_text(self):

+        original_date = rm.release_date_string
+        rm.release_date_string = lambda: "2099-01-02"
+        try:

+                    "# Demo 2.0.0 (2099-01-02)\n\nnew notes\n\n" + previous,
+                )
+        finally:
+            rm.release_date_string = original_date
+

+const setScrollGeometry = (el, { offset, clientSize, scrollSize, horizontal = false }) => {
+  const offsetKey = horizontal ? 'scrollLeft' : 'scrollTop'
+  const clientKey = horizontal ? 'clientWidth' : 'clientHeight'
+  const scrollKey = horizontal ? 'scrollWidth' : 'scrollHeight'
+
+  Object.defineProperty(el, offsetKey, {
+    configurable: true,
+    get () {
+      return offset
+    },
+    set (value) {
+      offset = value
+    }
+  })
+  Object.defineProperty(el, clientKey, {
+    configurable: true,
+    get () {
+      return clientSize
+    }
+  })
+  Object.defineProperty(el, scrollKey, {
+    configurable: true,
+    get () {
+      return scrollSize
+    }
+  })
+}
+
+const fireScroll = (wrapper, offset, options = {}) => {
+  const el = wrapper.vm.$el
+  setScrollGeometry(el, {
+    offset,
+    clientSize: options.clientSize === undefined ? 100 : options.clientSize,
+    scrollSize: options.scrollSize === undefined ? 400 : options.scrollSize,
+    horizontal: options.horizontal || false
+  })
+  const evt = new Event('scroll')
+  el.dispatchEvent(evt)
+  return evt
+}

+    patched = original
+    probe_path = (probe_dir / "SConscript").resolve()

+    if load_defaults in patched:
+        patched = patched.replace(

+            "    try:\n"
+            "        prereqs.load_defaults(platform_arm)\n"
+            "    except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except\n"
+            "        print('FIXTURE_PREREQ_BYPASS={}'.format(exc.__class__.__name__))",
+            1,
+        )
+
+    for marker in (
+        "Export('platform_arm', 'conf_dir')",
+        'Export("platform_arm", "conf_dir")',
+    ):
+        if marker in patched:
+            marker_line = next(line for line in patched.splitlines() if marker in line)
+            indent = marker_line[:len(marker_line) - len(marker_line.lstrip())]
+            probe_call = (

+                f"{indent}# Hidden-test probe for exported SCons environments.\n"
+                f"{indent}SConscript({str(probe_path)!r})\n"
+                f"{indent}Exit(0)"
+            )
+            modified = patched.replace(marker, marker + probe_call, 1)

+
+            Import('base_env', 'base_env_mpi')
+
+            orig_path = os.environ.get('PATH', '')
+            base_path = base_env.get('ENV', {}).get('PATH', '')
+            orig_first = orig_path.split(os.pathsep)[0] if orig_path else ''
+            base_first = base_path.split(os.pathsep)[0] if base_path else ''
+            fake_dir = os.environ.get('DAOS_HIDDEN_FAKE_MPI_DIR', '')
+            base_parts = base_path.split(os.pathsep) if base_path else []
+
+            print('ORIG_PATH_FIRST={}'.format(orig_first))
+            print('BASE_ENV_PATH_FIRST={}'.format(base_first))
+            print('BASE_ENV_HAS_FAKE_MPI_PATH={}'.format(fake_dir in base_parts))
+            print('BASE_ENV_MPI_IS_NONE={}'.format(base_env_mpi is None))

+            if base_env_mpi is not None:

+/* eslint-env mocha */
+const chai = require('chai')

+const fs = require('fs')
+const os = require('os')
+const path = require('path')

+const generateReport = require('../lib/cucumber-junit-report')
+
+const outDir = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'nwc-junit-report-test')
+
+let counter = 0
+function generate (featureOutput, options) {
+  counter += 1
+  const output = path.join(outDir, `report-${counter}.xml`)
+  generateReport(Object.assign({ output }, options), featureOutput)
+  return parse(fs.readFileSync(output, 'utf8'))
+}
+
+
+
+function parse (xml) {
+  const parser = sax.parser(true)
+  const suites = []
+  let suite
+  let testCase
+  parser.onopentag = (node) => {
+    const attrs = node.attributes
+    switch (node.name) {
+      case 'testsuite':
+        suite = { name: attrs.name, cases: [] }
+        suites.push(suite)
+        break
+      case 'testcase':
+        testCase = {
+          classname: attrs.classname,
+          name: attrs.name,
+          failure: null,
+          error: null,
+          skipped: false
+        }
+        suite.cases.push(testCase)
+        break
+      case 'failure':
+        testCase.failure = attrs.message || ''
+        break
+      case 'error':
+        testCase.error = attrs.message || ''
+        break
+      case 'skipped':
+        testCase.skipped = true
+        break
+    }
+  }
+  parser.write(xml).close()
+  return { suites }
+}
+
+function step (name, status, errorMessage) {
+  return {
+    keyword: 'Given ',
+    name,
+    match: { location: 'steps.js:1' },
+    result: errorMessage ? { status, error_message: errorMessage } : { status }
+  }
+}
+
+function scenario (name, steps) {
+  return { name, type: 'scenario', steps }
+}
+
+function feature (name, scenarios) {
+  return { name, elements: scenarios }
+}

+    time_index = _time_index(entity)

+    cutoff_times = rows[time_index].copy()
+    cutoff_times.iloc[0] = cutoff_times.iloc[0] + pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)
+    cutoff_times.iloc[1] = cutoff_times.iloc[1]
+    cutoff_times.iloc[2] = cutoff_times.iloc[2] + pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)
+    return pd.DataFrame({
+        'instance_id': rows[index].values,
+        'cutoff_time': cutoff_times.values,

+import sys
+import unittest
+import dataclasses
+from typing import Union
+
+from marshmallow import ValidationError
+
+from marshmallow_dataclass import class_schema
+
+if sys.version_info >= (3, 8):
+    from typing import Literal
+else:
+    from typing_extensions import Literal
+
+
+class TestLiteralField(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_class_schema_with_literal_does_not_error(self):
+        @dataclasses.dataclass
+        class A:
+            choices: Literal["x", "y"]
+
+
+        schema_cls = class_schema(A)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(schema_cls)
+
+    def test_literal_load_valid_value(self):
+        @dataclasses.dataclass
+        class A:
+            choices: Literal["x", "y"]
+
+        schema = class_schema(A)()
+        result = schema.load({"choices": "x"})
+        self.assertEqual(result, A(choices="x"))
+
+    def test_literal_load_other_valid_value(self):
+        @dataclasses.dataclass
+        class A:
+            choices: Literal["x", "y"]
+
+        schema = class_schema(A)()
+        result = schema.load({"choices": "y"})
+        self.assertEqual(result, A(choices="y"))
+
+    def test_literal_load_invalid_value_raises(self):
+        @dataclasses.dataclass
+        class A:
+            choices: Literal["x", "y"]
+
+        schema = class_schema(A)()
+        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
+            schema.load({"choices": "z"})
+
+    def test_literal_dump_valid_value(self):
+        @dataclasses.dataclass
+        class A:
+            choices: Literal["x", "y"]
+
+        schema = class_schema(A)()
+        result = schema.dump(A(choices="x"))
+        self.assertEqual(result, {"choices": "x"})
+
+    def test_literal_single_value_valid(self):
+        @dataclasses.dataclass
+        class A:
+            kind: Literal["only"]
+
+        schema = class_schema(A)()
+        result = schema.load({"kind": "only"})
+        self.assertEqual(result, A(kind="only"))
+
+    def test_literal_single_value_invalid_raises(self):
+        @dataclasses.dataclass
+        class A:
+            kind: Literal["only"]
+

+            schema.load({"kind": "other"})
+
+    def test_literal_int_does_not_coerce_string(self):
+
+
+
+        @dataclasses.dataclass

+

+`

+	}

+}
+
+func runAhoyForHelp(t *testing.T, config string, args ...string) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	goArgs := []string{"run", ".", "-f", config}
+	goArgs = append(goArgs, args...)
+	cmd := exec.Command("go", goArgs...)
+	var output bytes.Buffer
+	cmd.Stdout = &output
+	cmd.Stderr = &output
+	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
+
+
+		if !strings.Contains(output.String(), "COMMANDS:") &&
+			!strings.Contains(output.String(), "USAGE:") {
+			t.Fatalf("ahoy help command failed: %v\n%s", err, output.String())
+		}
+	}
+	return output.String()
+}
+
+func assertContains(t *testing.T, output, want string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if !strings.Contains(output, want) {
+		t.Fatalf("expected output to contain %q\nfull output:\n%s", want, output)
+	}
+}
+
+func assertInOrder(t *testing.T, output string, wants ...string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	offset := 0
+	for _, want := range wants {
+		index := strings.Index(output[offset:], want)
+		if index < 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("expected output to contain %q after byte offset %d\nfull output:\n%s", want, offset, output)
+		}
+		offset += index + len(want)
+	}
+}

+package eth
+
+import (
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+
+func pv(build [8]byte, major, minor, patch, prerelease uint32) ProtocolVersion {
+	return ProtocolVersionV0{Build: build, Major: major, Minor: minor, Patch: patch, PreRelease: prerelease}.Encode()
+}
+
+func TestProtocolVersionV0EncodeLayout(t *testing.T) {
+	build := [8]byte{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}
+	out := pv(build, 0x0a0b0c0d, 0x11121314, 0x21222324, 0x31323334)
+
+
+	require.Equal(t, byte(0), out[0], "version type must be 0")
+
+	for i := 1; i < 8; i++ {
+		require.Equal(t, byte(0), out[i], "reserved byte %d must be zero", i)
+	}
+
+	require.Equal(t, build[:], []byte(out[8:16]))
+
+	require.Equal(t, []byte{0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0d}, []byte(out[16:20]), "major")
+	require.Equal(t, []byte{0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14}, []byte(out[20:24]), "minor")
+	require.Equal(t, []byte{0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x24}, []byte(out[24:28]), "patch")
+	require.Equal(t, []byte{0x31, 0x32, 0x33, 0x34}, []byte(out[28:32]), "pre-release")
+
+	require.Len(t, out, 32)
+}
+
+func TestProtocolVersionString(t *testing.T) {
+	var zeroBuild [8]byte
+	opStack := [8]byte{'O', 'P', 's', 't', 'a', 'c', 'k'}
+	binBuild := [8]byte{0xff, 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06}
+
+	cases := []struct {
+		name string
+		v    ProtocolVersion
+		exp  string
+	}{
+		{"plain", pv(zeroBuild, 1, 2, 3, 0), "v1.2.3"},
+		{"zero version", pv(zeroBuild, 0, 0, 0, 0), "v0.0.0"},
+		{"prerelease", pv(zeroBuild, 1, 2, 3, 4), "v1.2.3-4"},
+		{"alphanumeric build", pv(opStack, 1, 2, 3, 0), "v1.2.3+OPstack"},
+		{"prerelease and build", pv(opStack, 1, 2, 3, 4), "v1.2.3-4+OPstack"},
+		{"binary build", pv(binBuild, 1, 2, 3, 0), "v1.2.3+0xff00010203040506"},
+		{"large numbers", pv(zeroBuild, 4000000000, 0, 0, 0), "v4000000000.0.0"},
+	}
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			require.Equal(t, c.exp, c.v.String())
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestProtocolVersionCompare(t *testing.T) {
+	var zb [8]byte
+	base := pv(zb, 2, 2, 2, 2)
+
+	require.Equal(t, Matching, base.Compare(pv(zb, 2, 2, 2, 2)))
+
+	require.Equal(t, AheadMajor, pv(zb, 3, 0, 0, 0).Compare(base))
+	require.Equal(t, OutdatedMajor, pv(zb, 1, 9, 9, 9).Compare(base))
+	require.Equal(t, AheadMinor, pv(zb, 2, 3, 0, 0).Compare(base))
+	require.Equal(t, OutdatedMinor, pv(zb, 2, 1, 9, 9).Compare(base))
+	require.Equal(t, AheadPatch, pv(zb, 2, 2, 3, 0).Compare(base))
+	require.Equal(t, OutdatedPatch, pv(zb, 2, 2, 1, 9).Compare(base))
+	require.Equal(t, AheadPrerelease, pv(zb, 2, 2, 2, 3).Compare(base))
+	require.Equal(t, OutdatedPrerelease, pv(zb, 2, 2, 2, 1).Compare(base))
+
+
+	require.Equal(t, AheadMajor, pv(zb, 3, 0, 0, 0).Compare(pv(zb, 2, 9, 9, 9)))
+
+
+	require.Equal(t, DiffBuild, pv([8]byte{'a'}, 5, 0, 0, 0).Compare(pv([8]byte{'b'}, 1, 0, 0, 0)))
+
+
+	require.Equal(t, EmptyVersion, base.Compare(ProtocolVersion{}))
+	require.Equal(t, EmptyVersion, ProtocolVersion{}.Compare(base))
+
+
+	typed := ProtocolVersion{}
+	typed[0] = 1
+	require.Equal(t, DiffVersionType, base.Compare(typed))
+	require.Equal(t, DiffVersionType, typed.Compare(base))
+
+
+	other := ProtocolVersion{}
+	other[0] = 1
+	other[31] = 9
+	require.Equal(t, InvalidVersion, typed.Compare(other))
+}
+
+func TestProtocolVersionJSON(t *testing.T) {
+	v := pv([8]byte{}, 1, 0, 0, 0)
+
+	data, err := json.Marshal(v)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+
+	expected := "\"0x" + hex.EncodeToString(v[:]) + "\""
+	require.Equal(t, expected, strings.ToLower(string(data)), "must encode as a 0x-prefixed 32-byte hex string")
+
+	var back ProtocolVersion
+	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(data, &back))
+	require.Equal(t, v, back, "JSON round-trip must preserve the value")
+
+
+	txt, err := v.MarshalText()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	var fromText ProtocolVersion
+	require.NoError(t, fromText.UnmarshalText(txt))
+	require.Equal(t, v, fromText)
+
+
+	var bad ProtocolVersion
+	require.Error(t, bad.UnmarshalText([]byte("0x1234")))
+}
